name: Vantablack Operations Thermal Coat
description:
A long insulated coat issued to Vantablack field personnel operating in cold-weather or extended outdoor conditions. The shell is a matte charcoal ripstop with a subtle corponation identifier woven into the collar lining — not a logo, just a thread pattern that reads under UV. Filled with a thin but highly effective synthetic insulation, the coat is warm without the bulk that would restrict movement or make it harder to access sidearms or equipment. Two deep hand pockets, a zippered chest pocket, and a sealed interior document pocket.

This coat signals Vantablack in a way that the average person recognizes without being able to articulate why. It's not branded. It's just cut a certain way, in a certain color, with a certain quality of fabric, worn by people who move with a certain economy. On the Gray Zone, seeing this coat means getting out of the way. In Tier 4 corridors, it means a meeting is happening that you're not part of.
functionality: Integrated front ballistic liner rated for standard rounds. UV-reactive thread identifier in collar lining for field recognition.
what_it_says: You work for Vantablack in a capacity that requires being outdoors for long periods, which means whatever you're doing is serious.
worn_by: corporate security contractors on outdoor assignment
anyone who's acquired one through unofficial channels and is either very brave or very stupid
story_hooks: A Vantablack Operations Thermal Coat shows up in a the Gray Zone secondhand market — Vantablack does not sell surplus, which means someone stripped it off a body or stole it from supply.
The UV-reactive identifier in this coat's collar is from a discontinued field unit — wearing it suggests either a very old coat or a very deep cover.
A contact reaches out wearing one of these coats but claims to have no affiliation with Vantablack — they want help and they won't explain the coat.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian long coat with a silhouette that reads as both corporate and operationally lean. The matte charcoal finish absorbs light, creating an almost shadowlike presence on the wearer. Cut to mid-thigh, designed for authority and accessibility rather than fashion. The coat's presence is imposing without being ostentatious—instantly recognizable to those who know what to look for.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight; allows full range of motion for field operations. Shoulders are set precisely for unimpeded arm movement. Torso accommodates layering and equipment without sagging. Cut to avoid bulk while maintaining thermal integrity.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte charcoal ripstop synthetic composite with a soft hand; lightweight yet durable ballistic weave. Interior lined with ultra-thin synthetic insulation rated for sub-zero conditions without added weight.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly muted finish with minimal sheen. The ripstop weave creates subtle grid texture visible only at close range. Collar lining has fine thread pattern (readable only under UV light) that indicates Vantablack affiliation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray, nearly black. No visible branding. The UV-readable thread pattern in collar lining is silver-toned but invisible to naked eye.
physical_description.closures: Full-length YKK magnetic fastener system disguised as traditional zipper teeth; friction-fit closure that operates silently. No audible clicks or mechanical sounds.
distinctive_features: Two deep hand pockets with reinforced seams for heavy equipment
Zippered chest pocket with weatherproof gasket
Sealed interior document pocket (thermal-sealed, not stitched)
UV-readable corponation identifier woven into collar lining—invisible to casual observation
Subtle weight distribution along interior suggests integrated sensor or tech compatibility
Cut designed for rapid access to concealed gear; side seams positioned to avoid snagging
Minimal visible stitching; edges appear sealed rather than sewn
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate issue; signals wealth and operational authority. The cost of the insulation and materials alone places this firmly in the upper echelon.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Vantablack field operatives, security contractors, and high-level corporate enforcement. Signals access, clearance, and the kind of authority that doesn't need explanation. Street-level recognition: a warning to keep distance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops a broken-in look with subtle creasing at elbows and shoulders after field use. Minor scuffs and contact marks accumulate but are nearly invisible against the matte finish. Well-maintained examples show no fraying or wear—this is a tool kept in working condition, not a fashion statement.
